record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For the two-dimensional global PEPS approximation problem, can the bond-dimension bound f(L) required to approximate an L × L system be chosen to grow polynomially in the linear system size L?

evidence.quote: Question 8 Can the function f(L) be taken polynomial in L?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional quantum spin system on an L × L square lattice, where each site carries a finite-dimensional Hilbert space of fixed dimension d. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) of bond dimension D on this lattice is a state obtained by placing, on each edge of the lattice, a maximally entangled pair of auxiliary D-dimensional systems and applying, at each vertex, a linear map from the four (or fewer, at the boundary) auxiliary D-dimensional spaces into the physical space C^d.

Suppose that for every L and every gapped local Hamiltonian H_L on the L × L lattice (with uniformly bounded local interactions and a uniform spectral gap), the unique ground state |ψ_L⟩ can be approximated to within a fixed error ε > 0 in trace distance by some PEPS of bond dimension at most f(L), for some function f: ℕ → ℕ.

Question: Can the function f(L) be chosen to grow at most polynomially in L?
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution was found. The question of whether 2D gapped ground states admit PEPS approximations with bond dimension polynomial in the linear system size L remains an active open problem; related work on area laws and approximability in 2D frustration-free systems makes partial progress but does not settle the polynomial-bond-dimension question.

status_evidence.title: An Area Law for 2D Frustration-Free Spin Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Whether ground states of locally gapped frustration-free systems can be approximated by efficiently representable tensor networks such as PEPS of small bond dimension is a natural open question.
status_evidence.claim: The polynomial-bond-dimension PEPS approximability of 2D gapped ground states is referenced as an open question in current literature.

status_evidence.title: Lecture Notes on Tensor Networks (Boulder School 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of PEPS approximation and bond dimension scaling in 2D, with the polynomial scaling question still presented as unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent lecture notes still treat the polynomial bond-dimension scaling for 2D PEPS approximations as an open issue.
